title: Black-box unstructured search with amplitude amplification

problem.task: Find a marked item among N items under a unique-solution promise.
problem.instance_distribution: All black-box predicates with exactly one marked input.
promises: N is a power of two.

input.representation: Coherent phase oracle for a Boolean predicate over log2(N) qubits.
assumptions: The phase oracle and its inverse are available coherently.

source.title: Strengths and weaknesses of quantum computing
source.note: Provides the oracle-model lower-bound context for unordered search.

contract.precondition: N is a power of two
contract.postcondition: The data register is uniform over all N indices

stages.operation: Alternate the phase oracle and diffusion reflection.

contract.precondition: Exactly one basis state is marked
contract.postcondition: The marked-state measurement probability is at least 2/3

stages.operation: Measure the data register and return its index.

contract.precondition: The marked-state probability is at least 2/3
contract.postcondition: The returned index is marked with probability at least 2/3

correctness_contract.precondition: The promises and black-box access contract hold.
correctness_contract.postcondition: The unique marked index is returned.
loop_invariants: The state remains in the two-dimensional good/bad subspace.

assumptions: Resource expressions are query-level estimates, not fault-tolerant costs.

proof_obligations.statement: Amplitude amplification rotates the initial state to marked overlap at least 2/3.
The algorithm uses O(sqrt(N)) oracle queries.
The quantum query upper bound is quadratically below the randomized query lower bound.
Construct and cost the coherent oracle for a concrete application.

claim.statement: Conditional on black-box oracle access, the candidate has a quadratic query advantage.

evidence.title: Quantum amplitude amplification and estimation
evidence.note: Supports the amplitude-amplification query upper bound.

evidence.title: Strengths and weaknesses of quantum computing

caveats: This does not establish a gate-level, fault-tolerant, or end-to-end speedup.
A concrete oracle may erase the query advantage after construction costs are included.
